utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [No interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, it's fine now. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat. Good morning to you all. The Court is in session. Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please, for today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-A, the Prosecution versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milan Lukic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, can you hear the proceedings and follow the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: I would like to have the appearances now, please, and I shall start with the representative of the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Matthew Gillett, appearing for the Prosecution together with Peter Kremer and our case manager, Colin Nawrot. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gillett. I'm now turning to the counsel of Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. Tomislav Visnjic and Dragan Ivetic on behalf of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Let me now turn to the counsel of Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of the Sredoje Lukic Defence team, myself, Djuro Cepic, as lead counsel and also appearing with me, Mr. Jens Dieckmann as co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to share with you today the fact that this Status Conference has been convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) and (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, which require that a Status Conference be held within 120 days of the filing of the Notice of Appeal, and then after that, 121 days after the previous Status Conference. The main purpose of such a Status Conference is to provide any person in detention pending an appeals judgement the possibility to raise questions relating to the latter, including his or her state of mental and physical health. Today it is the eighth Status Conference held as part of the appeals procedure in this case. The last Status Conference was held on the 23rd of January, 2012. The parties have accepted that this Status Conference be held outside the 121-day deadline with a view to meeting the availability of the counsel. I would like to tell you that we intend filing the appeals judgement before or immediately after the summer recess of 2012. Unfortunately, I am today unable to give you any further details relating thereto. I would now like to turn to Mr. Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic to ask them whether they have any questions relating to their conditions in detention or their state of health. Let me first turn to Mr. Milan Lukic. Would you like to share with me any concerns you may have regarding your conditions of detention or your state of health? THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] As far as the conditions in the Detention Unit are concerned, everything is fine. As far as my health is concerned, I do have certain health-related problems. That's been the case for seven years. I've been trying to prove that my eyes aren't blue. I have a document from the international court that states that I have blue eyes, tattoos, and a birth-mark on my face. That has never been the case, and as a result, I suffer to a large extent as a man. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have noted the concerns you have just addressed. Let me remind you that pursuant to Rules 80 and 81 of the Rules relating to conditions in detention, you may at any time submit a request to the commanding officer of the UNDU, and if necessary, to the Registrar. Let me now turn to Sredoje Lukic. Would you like to share with me any concerns you may have relating to your conditions of detention or relating to your state of health? THE APPELLANT S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all I would like to thank you for giving me the floor. There is nothing I have to say. Everything is fine, quite normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to thank you. You may sit down. I would finally like to ask the parties whether at this juncture they have any questions they would like to raise at this Status Conference. I shall first turn towards the representative of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We have no issues to raise today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gillett. Do the representative of -- or the counsel of Mr. Milan Lukic have any particular issue they would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no new issues that we would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Let me now turn to the counsel of Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Have you any particular issue you would like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Today nothing to raise, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. As far as I'm concerned, I have no further issues I wish to raise, and I therefore believe that the hearing can be adjourned. I would like to thank the parties for having attended this Status Conference, as well as all the staff of the Tribunal that has contributed to the organisation of this short Status Conference. The Court stands adjourned.
